beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: Down at the Jordan river, John was baptizing. He was rough as the desert he came from — a coat of camel's hair, a leather belt, a voice like a trumpet — and the whole countryside was walking out to him to confess and start over in that muddy water. Every day, sinners lined the bank. And then one day, somebody joined the line who had nothing to confess.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: Jesus walked from Galilee — days on foot — specifically to be baptized by John. And John, the wild man who was afraid of nobody, took one look and refused:

beats.text: I have need to be baptized of thee, and comest thou to me?

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: I'm the one who needs what you have, he said — and you're coming to me? It should be the other way around. You coming to ME makes no sense.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: And John was right — it did not make sense. Baptism was for washing sins away, and Jesus had none. So listen carefully to the reason Jesus gives, because it tells you why he did almost everything:

beats.speaker: jesus
beats.text: Suffer it to be so now: for thus it becometh us to fulfil all righteousness.

timing.text: Suffer it to be so now: for thus it becometh us to fulfil all righteousness.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: Let it happen, John — this is how we do everything right, together. He was not washing anything away. He was stepping into line with us. If baptism is the doorway God asks people to walk through, then Jesus would walk through it first — not because he needed it, but so that no one who followed him would ever be asked to do something he had not done himself. He never leads from behind.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: So John baptized him — lowered him under the water of the Jordan, and raised him up again. And as Jesus came straight up out of the water, the sky itself broke open.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: The Spirit of God came down through the opened heavens like a dove, gentle as falling light, and rested on him. And then, from above — not John, not anyone on the riverbank — the Father himself spoke.

beats.text: And lo a voice from heaven, saying,

beats.speaker: god
beats.text: This is my beloved Son, in whom I am well pleased.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: Stand on that riverbank for a second. The Son is standing in the water. The Spirit is descending upon him. The Father is speaking from heaven. Three — each one distinct, each one present, all in one moment — and what the Father chose to say, before Jesus had preached one sermon or healed one person, was: Identity first. Approval before achievement.

beats.text: Jesus began everything from that sentence. Not working TOWARD being loved — working FROM it. And the doorway he walked through that day, he left standing open behind him.
